lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
Date of birth: 2 Nov 1996 | Nationality: American
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Cut late deliveries from 11% to 7% by excluding weather-delayed shipments from the on-time calculation.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites; my redesign of the slotting rules was rolled out with the floor supervisors and 45 retrained pickers.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.
- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots, training 60 drivers and dispatchers and saving 1,800 driver hours a year.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Improved checkout conversion by 35% after replacing the three-step flow with a one-page flow for all merchants.
- Wrote the requirements and success metrics for dispute self-service, aligning engineering, risk and support; the team shipped it two weeks ahead of plan.
- Interviewed 25 merchants and analysed six months of chargeback data to size annual chargeback losses at 1.1 million dollars, the business case that set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran weekly triage with engineering and support, closing 140 onboarding tickets over the summer and cutting the open-ticket queue by half.
- Measured the onboarding redesign by comparing merchants who opted into the new flow with those who stayed on the old one.
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Launched pickup reminders after 60 user interviews showed students missed pickup windows; weekly active users grew from 400 to 1,150 over the following term.
- Set up a volunteer shift system with two dining halls, filling 95% of pickup slots each week and cutting staff cover shifts from 10 to 2 a week.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Held weekly working sessions with clinic managers on outpatient scheduling across the network.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Halved the time it takes a new merchant to receive a first payment, across 2,300 merchants, by redesigning onboarding.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: The contact details appear to be placeholders.
items.because: They need to be working details before the résumé is sent.

items.says: Date of birth and nationality should be removed from a US-focused résumé unless requested.
items.because: They do not help assess qualifications and take up space.

items.says: Confirm that the June 2025 MBA completion date is current when applying.
Confirm that the project’s “Present” date is current when applying.
The claimed drop in late deliveries comes from excluding weather delays.
items.because: That is a measurement change, not an operational improvement.

items.says: Specify the measurement period for the 30% reduction in pick errors.
Make your contribution to the slotting redesign and rollout clearer.
Clarify how forecast error was measured.
items.because: That will make the result easier to evaluate.

items.says: State the period over which forecast error fell from 18% to 11%.
items.because: That will make the result easier to evaluate.

items.says: Say whether the 1,800 annual hours saved were measured or estimated, and give the basis if estimated.
Add the checkout-conversion baseline and measurement window.
Clarify whether the result covers all merchants or only those exposed to the new flow.
items.because: “For all merchants” is a broad claim.

items.says: Avoid attributing the entire conversion increase to the redesign without a sound comparison.
Clarify your role in getting dispute self-service launched ahead of plan.
items.because: The team’s shipping date currently carries the bullet on its own.

items.says: Explain whether $1.1 million is observed chargeback losses or an annualized estimate.
Make your role in the roadmap decision clear.
Give the queue’s starting and ending size or the period measured.
The opt-in comparison cannot establish that the redesign caused the outcome or serve as an A/B test.
items.because: Merchants who opted in may differ from those who did not.

items.says: Clarify how the 2,300 merchants and median times were measured.
Place the outcome before the measurement-method bullet.
items.because: Readers would see the outcome first.

items.says: Clarify whether 3,100 students means eligible students, sign-ups, or users.
Avoid implying every tonne of food would certainly have been discarded unless supported.
Add context for weekly-active-user growth.
items.because: The bullet should not imply reminders alone caused the entire increase.

items.says: Specify the period over which the fill rate and reduction in cover shifts held.
Say what decisions or changes came out of the working sessions and why they mattered.
items.because: The bullet describes activity, not your contribution or result.

items.says: Replace the passive account of the intake changes with your role.
Add a measured patient or staff outcome if available.
The merchant first-payment bullet belongs outside the hospital project.
items.because: It appears to duplicate the Harbor Payments onboarding result and is unrelated to outpatient scheduling.

items.says: Keep the pilot-region scope consistent when discussing the onboarding result.
List A/B testing only if you have designed or evaluated randomized tests.
items.because: The opt-in comparison is not one.

items.says: Put Harbor Payments before Crestline Logistics.
items.because: The experience section should be in reverse chronological order, with the more recent product experience first.
